title: Enhanced recovery after cardiac surgery (ERACS) in interdisciplinary critical care medicine in the university heart center Bad Krozingen
summary:
Patients in the intensive care unit suffer not only from their underlying disease but also from the side effects of intensive medical measures. Traditional concepts assumed that the sedation of patients in the intensive care unit was indicated in order to shield patients from the stress of the often life-threatening situation and to allow them to tolerate intensive medical measures. Sedation induces side effects such as muscle breakdown due to immobilization (DOI: 10.1152/jappl.1997.82.1.182, DOI: 10.1002/ncp.10945). Further undesirable consequences of deep sedation include the need for airway management with consecutive mechanical ventilation and complications such as nosocomial pneumonia (DOI: 10.1186/s13054-019-2394-9).
Concepts for preventive measures have been established for intensive care patients (DOI: 10.1056/NEJMoa1906759, DOI: 10.1097/CCM.0000000000003299) and patients on or after extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO/ECLS, a system for temporary replacement of the heart and/or lungs, DOI: 10.1186/s13613-020-00776-3) and to mobilize them actively, for example. This means that physiotherapy is not limited to passive measures, but that patients are actively involved in their recovery, for example through breathing and mobilization therapy (DOI: 10.1097/CCM.0000000000003299).
The challenge of postoperative intensive care for awake patients is, in addition to adequate analgesia, the treatment of inadequate spontaneous breathing, especially when an endotracheal breathing tube is in place (DOI: 10.1056/NEJMoa1906759). On the one hand, there is wakefulness and physiological spontaneous breathing with active mobilization out of bed, and on the other hand, there is mechanical irritation of the respiratory tract (oral cavity, tongue, larynx including vocal cords, trachea) by the tube. A specific analgesia concept without sedation, supported by painless patient participation, supports the rehabilitation process. 
The concept of “sedation-free intensive care” was established at the Anesthesiology Intensive Therapy Station (AIT) of the Clinic for Anesthesiology and Intensive Care Medicine (KAI) at the University Medical Center Freiburg.
Since the merger of the University Heart Center Freiburg • Bad Krozingen with the University Hospital Freiburg in 2022, the concept of sedation-free intensive care has been implemented postoperatively for patients after cardiac surgery on the interdisciplinary operative intensive care ward (IOI/1E) by the Clinics for Anesthesiology and Intensive Care Medicine and Cardiovascular Surgery. This postoperative treatment has been established as one of three pillars in a multimodal, interdisciplinary and interprofessional approach under the term “Enhanced recovery after cardiac surgery” (ERACS). The postoperative goal for the patient is a prompt recovery and restoration of patient autonomy through early extubation and mobilization, effective postoperative analgesia and delirium management. In addition, the detection and treatment of delirium and postoperative pain, as well as the prevention of acute renal failure, are of primary importance. As a rule, early extubation is aimed for immediately after the end of the operation, in order to then begin rehabilitative measures in the intensive care unit.
The aim of the research project is to determine whether implementing the ERACS concept, which focuses on sedation-free intensive care, reduces the incidence of postoperative complications.
conditions: Does the implementation of the ERACS concept with a focus on sedation-free intensive care reduce the incidence of postoperative complications?

interventions.name: Cardiosurgical patient population before implementation of the Enhanced Recovery After Cardiac Surgery (ERACS) concept with sedation-free intensive care and incidence of organ complications

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Cardiac surgery with and without ECC and postoperative mechanical ventilation
- Comparison of 2019 to 2023/2024 (approx. 1,000 patients per year)
- Age at admission to hospital ≥18 years
- Admission to the interdisciplinary operative intensive care unit in Bad Krozingen
Exclusion criteria:
none
